messages:
mira: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak from the last canary we keep hitting recurring idle pockets on 8xA100 pipeline runs (seq=1024, global batch=32, microbatch=4). All-reduce fraction jumped on the hot path. Posting a tiny profiler excerpt below for step 120. :eyes:

```
[PROF] step=120 total=232ms compute=180ms comm=52ms all_reduce=48ms wait_kv=12ms
microbatch timeline (GPU0): Fwd[0..60ms] -> send_slice[60..80ms] -> wait_kv[80..92ms] -> Bwd overlap start[92ms] -> idle gap[140..180ms]

note: kernel-selector logs show fallback to fp32 GEMM on some layers when seq>512 (selector: chosen_kernel=fp32_slow GEMM).
```

aj: saw this too on the same canary. selector is picking a safer kernel for some fused-attn blocks; that increases compute but seems to alter how we slice tensors which balloons all-reduce sizes.

mira: exactly — compute itself isn't huge, but the tensor partitioning increases all-reduce bandwidth. The schedule loses overlap and we get those idle patches (pockets) between fwd/bwd.

sam: quick test: reducing microbatch from 4->2 reduced the idle patch on 4x runs, but throughput dropped so not a long-term fix. One-forward-one-back windowing (one-forward-one-back scheduling) with a smaller window gave better overlap for me.

lee: I pushed a WIP to the batching heuristics to bias toward fewer, slightly larger microbatches if kvcache.hit_rate>0.8 — PTAL: https://git/repo/branch (WIP).

kyle: perf-bot flagged a regression around 2026-03-08; bisect points at kernel-chooser commit abc123. cc @mira @aj.

perf-bot: [alert] perf regression detected: median p99 latency +12% on pp-8x-A100 profile suite after commit abc123.

mira: repro script for reproducing locally: `./bench_pp.sh --gpus=8 --seq=1024 --microbatch=4 --one-forward-one-back` — run with `KERNEL_DEBUG=1` to dump selector decisions.

aj: another angle — try prefetching KV earlier to hide wait_kv. Adding `kvcache.prefetch=true` shaved ~15ms off wait_kv in a quick run, but all_reduce still dominates.

samir: I ran an A/B: prefetch helped but only for small slices. The main cost is all-reduce of many small tensor slices; latency of many small allreduces >> single fused allreduce. We should test slice fusion (bigger slices) or reduce the number of slices by changing kernel tiling.

lee: I'll run an all-reduce fusion experiment today (fuse adjacent slices before reduce) and a variant that forces the kernel-selector to prefer the fp16高速 kernel (if safe). Will post numbers.

mira: thanks. next actions: (1) aj/lee try slice-fusion + kernel-selector override on canary, (2) sam run 1F1B windowing configs with different microbatch counts and report throughput/latency tradeoffs, (3) kyle coordinate a perf bisect to produce exact regression delta per layer.

ops-bot: deploy queued: canary/2026-03-09-21 -> infra-canary-8xA100. Monitor channel for errors. :rocket:

aj: FYI if fusion reduces number of allreduces we should also check CUDA IPC pressure and NIC coalescing (might shift bottleneck).

samir: noted — I'll capture NCCL traces + nvprof and attach in follow-up.

mira: great. if anyone gets a convincing fix quickly, we can hotfix kernel-selector; otherwise we'll carry the batching heuristic tweak to next canary. :thumbsup:
